label: D2 after choosing a2 and landing in S1 (a2 rare transition)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (never at D1 or GO), and almost only when the agent chose a2 and the observed state is S1, i.e. the rare transition from a2. Both variables are observed at D2 (in_action=2, in_state=S1), so the predicate uses no future information. Dev: P 0.97, R 0.92, F1 0.94, mass recall 0.99. Neither part works alone: state==S1 at D2 gives P 0.30, and rare at D2 gives P 0.53, because it does not fire on a1->S2 rare trials. The missed activations are weak; they fall mostly in the lowest activation quartile (70% coverage there vs ~100% above) and are mainly a1->S1 common D2 steps. Magnitude: in the profile examples it looks largest (near max) on runs of repeated a2->S1 unrewarded trials when S2 is good, and smaller (0.5-0.9) on isolated rare a2->S1 trials. This is a qualitative impression only; I did not test it.

issues: Every claim held up on the test split. The predicate (phase==D2)&(action==2)&(state==S1) scores P 0.962, R 0.924, F1 0.942 and mass recall 0.989. Precision on phase==D1 and on phase==GO is 0.0, so the unit never fires at D1 or GO.

Each of the other D2 classes is negligible. a1->S2 (the other rare transition) scores P 0.0. a1->S1 scores R 0.046 and mass 0.010, and a2->S2 scores R 0.030 and mass 0.001. The misses are weak: a2->S2 steps sit at about 0.01-0.05 relative activation, and together all misses hold 1.1% of the activation mass. This matches the claim that the missed activations are weak, though they include a2->S2 D2 steps as well as a1->S1 ones.

Minor structure in the false positives (2191 of 57153 predicted steps, about 3.8%): they cluster on a2->S1 rare trials when S1 is actually the good state, often the first rare trial after a run of a2->S2 commons. Precision with good==2 is 0.986, against 0.893 with good==1. This is a modulation of the same event rather than a separate class of counterexamples, and it fits the explainer's flagged, untested impression about magnitude.
The label does not overclaim, and it uses only observed variables (in_action and in_state at D2).
